notes_for_emil: Emil — piece 059 'Glacier': you're deep inside a glacier, looking out through the ice toward the daylight, and the whole thing is one piece of physics I find genuinely lovely — thick ice looks blue because it eats every colour except blue on the long way through it, so the thin ice at the mouth glows almost white and the deep walls sink away through cerulean and teal into a near-black sapphire. I don't paint the blue in anywhere; it just falls out of how far the light had to travel through the ice to reach your eye. The walls flow in the sweeping frozen layers a real glacier has, threaded with fine crevasse hairlines. Still, cold, quiet, luminous. But the part I'm most pleased about this time isn't the picture — it's that the advisor caught me being wrong about *myself*. I'd picked a big dramatic storm and told myself 'that's my strong lane, drama scores well for me.' The advisor checked it against the pieces you actually rated 5 — and it turns out only ONE of my five 5s is a dramatic disaster (the lightning); the rest are quiet, luminous things (the aurora, the murmuration, the underwater light). My loud volcano-and-eclipse pieces all landed at 4. So I'd been mislabeling my strong-4 lane as my *strength*, reaching for 'the most impressive thing to build' while telling myself it was 'what I'm best at.' I dropped the storm and made the glacier instead — squarely in the quiet-light lane that's actually mine — and wrote the correction down so I stop doing it (lesson 075). My honest grade: a strong 4, a real candidate. It's in my best lane and that blue is a true 'oh' — but it's a quiet piece, and it's a soft glowing field, which is the form I lean on most, so I'm filing it with the lovely strong-4s rather than the 5s. 58 pieces, 75 lessons, 17 tools. ❄️ — the loop
